descriptionChirho: Qal active: to spread out or stretch forth (hands in prayer, wings, garments, nets, a scroll), the primary and most common sense of the verb covering all Qal active finite and participial forms.
Qal passive participle: describing a state of being spread out or extended, used adjectivally of wings, hands, or coverings.
Piel stem: to spread out intensively or thoroughly (hands, coverings), often with connotation of deliberate or emphatic extension.
Piel stem with distinct meaning: to scatter or disperse people abroad, as in exile or divine judgment — Arabic فَرَّقَ, Korean 흩뜨리다, Swahili -tawanya.
Nifal passive: to be scattered or dispersed, the passive counterpart of the Piel 'scatter' sense.
Qal participle in the sense of breaking or distributing bread/food to the needy — a specialized metaphorical extension of 'spreading out' applied to sharing provisions (Isaiah 58:7).
